text:
Maya P: ran an nsys capture against the low-latency path this morning, grabbing both cuda and host traces. weird pattern: memcpy launched on stream 3, kernel on stream 7, but there's a 30-60ms wallclock lull between them on the host timeline
Oliver C: can you paste the timeline screenshot or a short waterfall snippet?
Maya P: pasted snippet below (trimmed)
```
# nsight timeline excerpt (timestamps in us)
stream 3: H2D memcpy 0.12ms -> 0.15ms
CPU: scheduling gap 30000us (thread sleeping)
stream 7: kernel conv_fwd 0.35ms -> 0.8ms
stream 3: H2D memcpy 0.13ms -> 0.16ms (later job)
```
Kai R: hmm host gap 30ms is suspiciously like the batching timer firing window. are we coalescing requests and then sleeping?
Maya P: batching config is aggressive: commit_after 8ms, max_wait 25ms. I thought that would keep gaps low, but traces show CPU thread goes idle and only wakes to queue the kernel.
Anya S: do we see any memcpy queued on the copy engine that then stalls waiting for host-side work? can you filter by memcpy start vs enqueue?
Maya P: yes — enqueue happens, but actual cudaMemcpyAsync seems delayed until after host wake. I suspect host thread preempted by something else (kworker / snapshot job).
perf-bot: automated note: recent perf regression detected on canary; p50 token latency +12% vs baseline after 2026-02-18 deploy. See perf:ci/5872
Oliver C: timeline overlap check: are memcpys and kernels in same CUDA context but different streams? if the kernel uses default stream semantics or kernel launches are serialized by stream priorities that could explain ordering.
Maya P: they're separate streams, priorities default. I traced stream IDs: memcpy on stream 3 (Copy Engine), kernel on stream 7 (Compute). nsight shows copy engine activity but the copy calls don't appear to actually start until host thread wakes.
Kai R: that points to host-side submission latency. On Linux, if the submit helper thread is preempted, cuda runtime only enqueues work when user thread calls the API. do you have perfetto or ftrace showing the syscall timings?
Maya P: ran perf record of the worker thread. saw long nanosleep and a few SCHED_OTHER preemptions around the same timeframe. attaching sample lines:
```
# perf sample (truncated)
comm: batch_dispatcher tid:2345
  sched: sleep 30ms
  wake: 2ms syscall submit_cuda
  userspace: cudaMemcpyAsync() -> returns
```
Anya S: interesting. Could be our batching timer + pthread_cond_wait dropping into kernel and being preempted by GC-ish housekeeping. Which kernel module/process was active at the time?
Maya P: kswapd showed short CPU bursts; also docker logrotate cron at exact minute (ugh).
Oliver C: ops aside, how actionable for runtime? two knobs: 1) switch to busy-wait short spin before sleeping (trade CPU for lower tail). 2) pin the worker thread to isolated CPU or SCHED_FIFO with low nice.
Kai R: also consider moving critical submission path to an io_uring thread or use cudaLaunchHostFunc to decouple submission so host sleep less likely to block kernel start. Might be heavy.
Maya P: quick experiment: increased batch commit_after to 0 (immediate) for a canary, saw tail latency drop but overall CPU utilization up ~6%. timeline gaps disappeared.
Anya S: did you re-run nsys after that change to confirm memcpy/kernels overlap improved?
Maya P: yes — new trace shows memcpy start immediately followed by kernel with ~200us gap only (dispatch overhead). Streams now overlap as expected.
perf-bot: automated note: repeat capture recommended with NVTX ranges around batch boundaries for clarity.
Oliver C: long term we should: (a) change worker thread scheduling (b) add NVTX around batching logic, (c) update docs to avoid cronjobs on GPU hosts during canary windows.
Kai R: also add a microbenchmark in CI that validates no host-sleep >5ms observed under synthetic load.
Maya P: creating a follow-up issue with traces + perf profile. I'll include the nsys CLI I used:
```
nsys profile --output=run_2954321000 --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=timeline --capture-range=kernel --force-overwrite ./bench_node --args "--profile-mode" 
```
Anya S: ack, please include a short repro script that toggles batching timers so SRE can run on dedicated infra.
Maya P: will do. tagging SRE: @Oliver C please help coordinate a host window for a pinned-cpu run.
Oliver C: happy to, will book a slot and test SCHED_FIFO vs cpuset binding.
Kai R: one last thought: check kernel selection path for small-batch fallback — we've seen a codepath that compiles different kernels if batch < N and that path incurs extra kernel prep on host which could be serializing.
Maya P: good call — I'll grep for host-side code that builds kernel params on different thread and try to inline for small batches.
Anya S: nice work. keep the traces linked in the ticket. :thumbsup:
Maya P: thanks all, filing ticket now with the trace tarball and short TL;DR.
